name: MeleePad
game: Super Smash Bros. Melee (GameCube, GALE01 USA v1.00 or v1.02)

inputs.description: Your own reviewed GALE01 USA v1.00 or v1.02 disc image; the backend checks its full hash and extracts it privately. Native Slippi online play needs v1.02 and a separate developer build.

command:
import json,plistlib,sys
v=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
p=sys.argv[2]+'/Contents/Info.plist'
with open(p,'rb') as f: info=plistlib.load(f)
info['CFBundleShortVersionString']=v['version']
info['CFBundleVersion']=str(v['build'])
with open(p,'wb') as f: plistlib.dump(info,f)

tools.name: xcodebuild
tools.note: Install full Xcode and its iOS platform; select Xcode's command-line tools in Xcode Settings > Locations, then run PadMint again.

tools.name: xcrun
tools.label: Xcode iOS SDK
tools.note: Install full Xcode and its iOS platform; select Xcode's command-line tools in Xcode Settings > Locations, then run PadMint again.

tools.name: rustup
tools.label: Rust 1.88.0
tools.note: Install Rustup, then run: rustup toolchain install 1.88.0 --target aarch64-apple-ios

tools.name: xcrun
tools.label: macOS command-line SDK
tools.note: Install Apple Command Line Tools with xcode-select --install, then run PadMint again. Full Xcode is optional for this iPhone module build.

tools.name: %ProgramFiles(x86)%/Microsoft Visual Studio/Installer/vswhere.exe
tools.label: Visual Studio C++ Build Tools
tools.note: Install Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools with Desktop development with C++ and a Windows SDK. On Windows ARM64, add the ARM64 C++ tools (preferred) or the x64/x86 C++ tools.

notes: PadMint compiles the offline game module and stages it with its matching DOL-identity sidecar into the published app. The selected revision keeps its existing gGALE01_recomp.dylib or gGALE01r2_recomp.dylib name. Requires schema 2 module-result support; do not release this recipe before that PadMint support ships. The macOS and Slippi developer build paths are unchanged.

publication.reason: The release publishes the app without game code; PadMint adds the module translated from the player's own disc, which stays personal.
